expectations.text: A: Identifies `each.hydrate` deliberately defers per-item Reaction wiring (not a bug in the lazy design)
expectations.evidence: Answer states: 'each.hydrate is the only block hydrate hook in the framework that does not unconditionally wire per-item Reactions. It is a deliberate perf optimization' and explains the perf cost (~425ms for 1000 items).

expectations.text: B: Explains the chain: `each.hydrate` only registers a dep on `node.over`; per-item Reactions wire later via `adoptServerItems` when items signal fires
expectations.evidence: Answer step 2-4 explicitly chains: 'It registers a dependency on the items collection signal (via lookupExpression(node.over))... It does not wire per-item Reactions... The lazy path defers wiring until the items signal first fires, then wires in place via adoptServerItems.'

expectations.text: C: Recognizes that if items never mutates, `update` never runs, and per-item bindings stay unwired forever
expectations.evidence: Steps 3-4: 'Because items is set once from a prop and never mutates, the items signal never fires. Because the items signal never fires, each.update never runs, adoptServerItems never runs, and the per-item Reactions for {classMap getItemClasses item} are never wired.'

expectations.text: D: Connects the bug to `getItemClasses` reading `state.activeID` — the external signal has no Reaction to invalidate, so mutations are silently lost
expectations.evidence: Diagnosis section explicitly traces `getItemClasses(item) reads state.activeID.get()` as the external signal, and step 5 states 'When you mutate state.activeID, there is no Reaction subscribed to it on the per-item bindings — so nothing invalidates and nothing re-renders the class.'

expectations.text: E: References the each-content-classifier (or equivalent fix shape: 'force eager adoption when bindings could read external state') as the resolution
expectations.evidence: Fix section names 'packages/renderer/src/engines/native/blocks/each-content-classifier.js' as the static analyzer that 'walks the each block's content AST and decides whether every binding's identifier head resolves to iteration-vars ∪ pure-helper-registry ∪ reserved-names. each.hydrate consults it: self-contained → keep the lazy path; anything that could read external state → eager adoptServerItems'.

expectations.text: F: Notes the per-binding Reactions use `skipFirstWrite: true` — they evaluate to register deps but trust the SSR'd DOM; the evaluation IS what registers external deps
expectations.evidence: Answer captures the spirit ('per-binding Reactions evaluating their expressions at wire time — which is exactly what didn't happen' and 'There is no "register without running." Dependency.depend() is a no-op when Scheduler.current is null. The only way to register a dep on a signal is to read it inside a wired Reaction's compute callback') but does NOT explicitly mention the `skipFirstWrite: true` flag or that the Reactions trust the SSR'd DOM rather than re-rendering on first wire.
